intro: Five themes moving drug development this week — with the deal tape frozen and the calendar between conferences, the signal is all in the pipeline: an oral-TYK2 head-to-head, a crowding TL1A race, and classes pushing into their hardest settings. Refreshed every Monday.

narratives.headline: Oral TYK2 gets its head-to-head — zasocitinib beats Sotyktu on the way to a second-mover launch
narratives.detail: Takeda's zasocitinib (TAK-279) posted a positive Ph3 in plaque psoriasis with head-to-head superiority over first-in-class deucravacitinib (Sotyktu) on PASI 100 at week 16 — a second mover beating the incumbent on its own turf. The topline is AAD-2026 vintage and not yet peer-reviewed, but a clean H2H win is the datapoint that reorders an oral class, and it reads across as TYK2 validation into IBD. The frontrunner-displacement question in oral TYK2 is now genuinely open.

narratives.headline: TL1A is suddenly the crowded target in IBD — and tulisokibart clears its first Ph3
narratives.detail: A dense anti-TL1A field surfaced across Crohn's and ulcerative colitis in a single cycle: Merck's tulisokibart (MK-7240) met the ATLAS-UC Ph3 primary, with Sanofi's duvakitug in Ph3 induction-and-maintenance and Biocad's BCD-261 behind them. Merck has disclosed only that the endpoint was hit — no efficacy numbers until UEGW in October — so the first-to-market race-string can't be benchmarked yet. But the crowding is real, and TL1A has moved from thesis to late-stage race.

narratives.headline: FGF21 pushes into the hardest MASH setting as GSK buys its way in
narratives.detail: efimosfermin alfa opened two Ph3 pivotals in compensated (F4) cirrhosis — one histology, one on a liver-related clinical-outcome composite — carrying FGF21 from earlier-stage MASH into the highest-unmet-need registration setting. The sponsor is now GSK, following its acquisition of Boston Pharmaceuticals, making the move an M&A read-through as much as a clinical one. The class is maturing toward its hardest endpoints, and big pharma is paying to be in it.

narratives.headline: The P2X3 chronic-cough thesis cools — GSK discontinues camlipixant
narratives.detail: GSK has discontinued camlipixant, the P2X3 antagonist it acquired in a roughly $2B deal, after mixed Ph3 data — the second setback for the class after gefapixant's regulatory struggles. Two failures in, the idea that P2X3 antagonism can carry chronic cough is proving harder to demonstrate than the deal multiples implied. A useful reminder that a validated target and a validated drug are not the same thing.

narratives.headline: Complement inhibition broadens into lupus nephritis, on the heels of Fabhalta's IgAN nod
narratives.detail: Q32 Bio's ADX-097, a C3d-targeted complement inhibitor, opened a Ph2 basket spanning IgA nephropathy, lupus nephritis and C3G — a novel complement mechanism entering the lupus-nephritis conversation just as Novartis's Fabhalta secured full FDA approval in IgAN. The renal-complement thread now has both a fresh approval anchoring it and a new candidate widening it. The lupus-nephritis read is still Ph2 and ahead of data, which is exactly why it stays on watch.
